_doc: Daily drop: one thing for each crew member to open per flight day. Tier is rolled per ship and day from the voyage key (lv/engage.py); items in a tier come round in order with a per-ship offset, so nobody sees a repeat until the tier runs out. Rare items can carry 'art' (an artifact id in collections.json). {A} = your astronaut. STUBS: the content pass replaces these. House style: content/STYLE.md.

items.t: MEMO 0412. Crews are reminded that the galley clock is the reference clock. The other clocks are opinions.
Hull temperature sensor 14 reported -270 °C for one sample, then went back to normal. Logged. Not discussed.
A letter from home, three days in the uplink queue. The dog has learned to open the fridge. Nobody knows how, and the dog isn't saying.
Starbase: 31 °C, wind from the southeast, and a gull loose in the high bay again. Ground crew morale is described as 'fine'.
Ticket 2231 is closed by the ground as 'cannot reproduce'. {A} reproduces it twice before lunch and reopens it with a video.
Today's uplink: 14 procedure updates, 2 software patches, 1 crossword. The crossword gets done first.
The star tracker logs a faint object it can't match to any catalogue. Ground says it's probably ice from the last vent. Probably.
A recording from the launch-day control room. Fourteen people talking at once, all saying the same thing: go.
Mission Control approves 40 extra minutes of bandwidth for personal calls this week. The approval took six signatures and a meeting.
An envelope from the first crewed Starship flight, marked 'open past halfway'. Inside: a mission patch with one scorched corner, and four words. It gets quieter. Breathe.
A data card from the ground team: all seven ships on the pad the night before launch, lit from below. Someone has written the ship numbers on in pen.
The relay passes on a carrier tone from a probe that left Earth half a century ago. Still talking. The fleet is the closest anyone has been to it in decades.
